tossups.text: Ruthie loses her stuffed giraffe and wets herself while her mother Kate searches for a brown doll in a story titled for this character by Sarah Shun-lien Bynum. In another story, the narrator imagines freeing the women who this character has turned into birds after strangling him with his own hair. In Pale Fire , Charles Kinbote quotes "ret woren ok spoz on nat ut yett" as the first line of the Zemblan translation of a poem about this character. A story titled for this character was collected after "Puss-in-Boots" and before "The Snow Child" in The Bloody Chamber . In a poem, this character tempts a boy with "pretty games" and "garments of gold" before ultimately declaring "if you're not willing, my force I'll employ." A father asserts "be calm, stay calm" and "it's a streak of fog" to dismiss his son's repeated sightings of this character, but by the end of the poem he finds his son dead at the hands of character. For 10 points, name this supernatural title character of a Johann Wolfgang von Goethe poem that was set to music by Franz Schubert.

This deity was often thought by ancient writers, such as Artapanus of Alexandria, to have been incarnated as Moses. In one tale, this deity sends seven scorpions to protect Isis; in another. this deity helps heal Horus after he is stung by a different scorpion. In Greek times, this god was syncretized with Hermes in the form of Hermes Trismegistus and had a cult center at Hermopolis. To help Nut give birth, this god played senet against Khonsu and won 5 days worth of additional light. This god, who assists Anubis in weighing the hearts of the dead, has a beak that represents the crescent moon. For 10 points, name this ibis-headed Egyptian god of magic, writing and knowledge.

Tulsidas composed a 40-verse chalisa hymn to this deity, who was born after an offering of sacred pudding flew into the hands of his mother. Before one journey, Jambavan had to give a reminder of this deity's strength. This child of Anjana is technically a vanara in his most common form, just like Vali and a king he advises named Sugriva. This god got a healing herb by changing size to lift a mountain. This god with a scarred chin is the son of Vayu. As a child, this god mistook the sun for a mango, and he later destroyed Ravana's fortress on Lanka as a fire burned on his tail. For 10 points, name this helper of Rama, a Hindu monkey god.

The Mytilenean general Pittacus placed ladders at temples of this Greek deity to allow her to climb up and down as she pleased. A cult in the Hellenistic era in the city of Itanos on Crete worshiped this deity Protogenia alongside Zeus Soter. A swimmer at the feet of a statue of this deity by Eutychides symbolized the Orontes river in the newly founded city of Antioch. This deity was depicted as the consort of a household serpentine deity who came to be the protector of Alexandria, the Agathos Daimon. Often donning a mural crown, she is depicted holding Plutus and a cornucopia, or a ship's rudder. Alexander the Great held in high esteem, for 10 points, what goddess of luck?

SYNE1 ("sign-one") and SYNE2 ("sign-two") code for actin-binding proteins found in this structure, which is bounded by the LINC complex. This structure is the location of a protein that interacts with Torsin A and is known as LAP1. One protein complex found on this structure is formed of proteins lined with FG repeats that interact with Kaps. Mutations in proteins that associate with this structure cause Emery-Dreifuss muscular dystrophy. This structure is lined with octagonally symmetric structures formed of nups; those complexes contain a basket-shaped structure facing this structure's lumen. Maturation-promoting factor promotes the dissolution of this structure, whose interior is lined with type V intermediate filaments. The Ran cycle provides the GTP required for importin and exportin to transport proteins through this structure. For 10 points name this structure that surrounds the lamina and the genetic information of the cell.

Springer Mountain is the southern end of an important entity in these mountains, and subranges of this mountain range include the Black, Catskill, and Pocono Mountains. Mount Katahdin is the northern terminus of its namesake trail, and Mount Mitchell, the highest point east of the Mississippi, is found in this range. For 10 points, name this mountain range running the entire eastern coast of the United States.

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for esophagus and swallowing. It plays a key role in the digestive system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this esophagus-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The esophagus is a key component of the Digestive system, involved in esophagus and swallowing.

tossups.text: After a massacre at the end of this novel, the title character's preaching causes his nephew to force him onto the shore of China. Earlier in this novel, a Portuguese captain rescues the titular character from the seaport of Sallee ("suh-LEE"). The title character of this novel also teaches English to Friday. For 10 points, name this novel, depicting a lost Englishman, written by Daniel Defoe.

This organization runs the Term Auction Facility and the Term Securities Lending Facility. This institution was established after the Panic of 1907 caused J.P. Morgan to bail out several banks, and its Board of Governors serve on its namesake "Open Market Committee." This organization purchased bank assets to increase the money supply after the 2008 financial crisis in quantitative easing period, which was led by Ben Bernanke. U.S. monetary policy is developed by, for 10 points, what central banking system currently led by Janet Yellen?

A model for this process was titled for Josef Stefan and James Maxwell after they independently developed equations for this process in multicomponent systems. The flux of this phenomenon is equal to a namesake coefficient times the negative concentration gradient according to the first of Fick's laws. This process can be modeled as a random walk, and it is caused by particle collisions. For 10 points, name this chemical process in which molecules move from high-concentration areas to low-concentration areas.

A leader in this country declared "Come, you pack of morphine addicts" to occupying forces in the so-called San Albino manifesto. This country's government hired retired American generals to form the Guardia Nacional to avoid using private armies. A guerilla war in this country waged by a general known for oversized cowboy hats helped the exiled president Juan Bautista Sacasa return to power. The Constitutionalist War in this country led to an American intervention after the deposition of Emiliano Chamorro. A rebel leader in this country gave his name to a leftist group led by Daniel Ortega which deposed Anastasio Somoza. For 10 points, name this country that experienced a civil war in the 1980s between the Contras and the Sandinistas.

A 2016 exhibition of this artist's "Visions of Genius" at the Noordbrabants Museum authenticated a depiction of St. Anthony separated from a funnel by a river. The burning of this artist's hometown may have inspired several blackened buildings in the background of his paintings. This artist depicted a man dropping coins into a chest as a skeleton pokes through a door and points a silver arrow at a man in bed. Joan Miró's The Tilled Field was inspired by a painting by this artist in which birds appear gifting strawberries. This artist may have depicted himself as a pale white "tree man" who appears below a knife squished by two ears in a chaotic "Hell scene." For 10 points, name this Dutch artist of The Garden of Earthly Delights.

Hepcidin (HEP-sid-in) prevents the export of this element from the cell. Siderophores (sid-ER-uh-forz) such as enterobactin (ent-ER-uh-bak-tin) are used by bacteria to sequester this element. Redox reactions in the electron transport chain are mediated by clusters of sulfur and this element, which are also found in the Krebs cycle enzyme aconitase (uh-KAHN-it-ayz). This element is coordinated to porphyrin (POR-feer-in) in a molecule that forms part of a protein with 210 times greater affinity for carbon monoxide than oxygen. For 10 points, name this element whose presence in heme (heem) gives blood its metallic taste.

In chromatography, these molecules are stained by aniline hydrogen oxalate. One of these molecules called Ficoll ("FAI-cawl") is used to separate the components of blood. In a form of affinity chromatography, these molecules bind to concanavalin A. A continuous gradient of one of these molecules is used to separate polyribosomes via centrifugation. A mixture of sodium citrate, anhydrous sodium carbonate, and copper sulfate makes up Benedict's reagent, which reacts with these molecules when they have free aldehyde or ketone groups. Haworth projections are used to display the cyclic configurations of these molecules, whose monomers usually have carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen in a 1-to-2-to-1 ratio. For 10 points, name these macromolecules that include starch and glucose.

A book whose title starts with this word opens with its author explaining how cold snaps during his childhood in Houston led him to picture God walking towards him down a dirt road. This word begins the title of a book in which the author meets a Hopi medical student, a maple syrup farmer, and a prostitute in rural Nevada while on a circle-shaped, 13,000-mile route avoiding all major interstates and cities. In a memoir with a title beginning with this word, the author finds herself unable to rise from her chair while watching Vanessa Redgrave rehearse for a one-woman show based on the author's previous book. In a memoir set in Oregon, the author is reminded of aspects of his faith while watching a jazz musician mention this adjective on TV while he audits humanities classes at Reed. "Highways" described by this word title a road trip travel narrative by William Least Heat-Moon, while this adjective and the word "jazz" appear in a Christian memoir by Donald Miller. This color appears in the title of a memoir about the death of the author's daughter Quintana Roo, intended as a companion piece to The Year of Magical Thinking. For 10 points, "Nights" of what color title a grief memoir by Joan Didion?

A relatively high value for this quantity in deep eutectic solvents results in high solubility of ionic compounds in them, and in high performance liquid chromatography, this property determines the elution order of solutes. Covalent compounds with this property have electronegativity values between 0.4 and 1.7 on the Pauling scale, and this property is responsible for the formation of hydrogen bonds between water molecules. For 10 points, name this property, in which two ends of a molecule have opposite electrical charges.

this structure is essential for partial pressure gradients. It plays a key role in the respiratory system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this diffusion-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The diffusion is a key component of the Respiratory system, involved in partial pressure gradients.

tossups.text: 2. The Marr-Albus theory applies to this human organ; though located in the medulla oblongata, the inferior olives provide inputs to this organ, so do mossy fibers. Three lobes can be seen in this organ, and the vermis is located between the two hemispheres of this organ. Some of the largest neurons, the Purkinje cells, and the smallest, the granule cells, are found here. Lesions in this organ can cause dysmetria or other forms of ataxia, which are mostly motor-related. For 10 points, identify this organ located just below the cerebrum in humans whose name means "little brain" in Latin.

A canteen girl named Marie is adopted by a group of these people in a Donizetti opera. In another opera, one of these people drowns in a lake under a blood-red moon after killing his wife, and is named Wozzeck [["VOT-seck"]]. Almaviva disguises himself as a drunken one of these people to woo Rosina in The Barber of Seville. In another opera, a man in this profession receives a flower from Micaëla in front of the cigarette factory. That character, Don José, stabs a woman who described her love as a "rebellious bird" in the Habanera. For 10 points, name this profession of many characters from Carmen and The Daughter of the Regiment, the latter of which is set in the Napoleonic Wars.
acceptableAnswers: equivalents and descriptions like “being in the military”

tossups.text: In a story from this country, Athena Hopballehus resists the advances of Boris before a prioress transforms into the title Monkey. A cook spends her lottery winnings on a "real French dinner" for Martina and Philippa in another story from this country. After the splinters of a troll mirror freeze Kai's heart, Gerda saves Kai from the title Snow Queen in a story by an author from this country. A girl exchanges her voice for human legs to win over a prince in a story by an author from this country who also wrote "The Ugly Duckling." A statue of the Little Mermaid honors Hans Christian Andersen in, for 10 points, what country's capital of Copenhagen?

parts.text: This author of "Tell Them Not to Kill Me!" created the greatest Pedro of them all, the rascally title character of Pedro Páramo.
Aunt Matilde disappears from Pedro's house in "The Walk," a short story by this South American novelist, who also wrote the novels Coronation and A House in the Country.
This Spanish playwright, whose first name is Pedro, wrote such works as Devotion of the Cross and Life is a Dream.

bonuses.leadin: Name these authors who love the name Pedro, For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Egyptian god of the moon.
The 365-day calendar came about after this god successfully gambled against Khonsu for five extra days. This Egyptian god of wisdom and writing is usually depicted with the head of an ibis.
Thoth gambled with Khonsu so that this goddess of the sky would be able to give birth to Osiris, Set, and Isis.

bonuses.leadin: Along with his mother Mut and father Amun, this god forms the Theban Triad. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Give this name of two chieftains, the sons of Telamon and Oileus. One of them committed suicide after going mad and slaughtering cattle and sheep, under the impression that they were Greek generals.
This man was awarded the armor of Achilles and thus earned the ire of Ajax the Greater. He would later face a difficult journey home to Ithaca and his wife Penelope after the Trojan War.

Along with Diomedes, Odysseus stole this statue of Athena from the Trojans, believing that its theft would hasten the end of the war. It was later brought to Rome by Aeneas and kept in the Temple of Vesta.

bonuses.leadin: One man with this name was killed after boasting to Poseidon that he could not be drowned. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this author of Blindness and Insight: Essays in the Rhetoric of Contemporary Criticism.
Paul de Man was one of the leading proponents of this school of literary analysis in America. Its French proponents included Jacques Derrida.
Derrida's Of Grammatology popularized the term "logocentrism" to describe the ethnocentric privilege that Western cultures give to this method of communication over all other forms of communication.

bonuses.leadin: This Yale professor analyzed the "Figural Language" in authors like Proust and Rousseau in his text, Allegories of Reading. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This is the reaction of polymerization linking the C-terminus of one amino acid to the N-terminus of the next and releasing water in the process.
The aforementioned reaction forms these bonds between amino acids that make up a protein.

In this solid-phase synthesis, the C-terminus of the next amino acid to be added to the chain is protected to prevent undesired polymerization. Abbreviated as Boc, tert-Butoxycarbonyl is the traditional protecting group of the carbonyl in this form of synthesis.

bonuses.leadin: Identify the following about the linking of amino acids for 10 points each:

parts.text: The Knights Hospitaller ruled this island until they were kicked out by Ottoman sultan Suleiman the Magnificent. A massive statue of the sun god Helios on this island was called its "colossus."
This island is the second most populous of the Balearic Islands, after Majorca (mah-YOR-kah). This island is a popular Spanish tourist destination, and is particularly known for its EDM scene.
Archimedes lived on this island, where he legendarily defended its largest city, Syracuse, against Roman invaders using a heat ray. Mount Etna lies on this largest island in Italy.

bonuses.leadin: Name these Mediterranean islands, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with lung volumes and capacities.
What is the main function of the diaphragm in the respiratory system?
Name another component of the respiratory system related to lung volumes and capacities.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human respiratory system.

parts.text: Give this surname shared by Victorian poets Robert and Elizabeth Barret.
In Robert Browning's "My Last Duchess," the narrator talks about his former wife as depicted in one of theseartworks. In an Oscar Wilde novel, one of these artworks ages in the place of Dorian Grey.
Elizabeth Barret Browning wrote this poetry collection, which includes poems such as "Yes, call me by mypet-name!" and "How do I love thee? Let me count the ways."

bonuses.leadin: An author with this surname wrote about a woman who had "a heart too soon made glad" in "My LastDuchess." For ten points each,

parts.text: Name this set of an individual's behavioral characteristics, divided by one theory into Type-A and Type-B.
This projective personality test involves interpreting 10 cards with ink blots of various colors printed on them.
This school of psychology stressed the "whole" personality over tests of its parts. Founded by Max Wertheimer, it included Kurt Koffka, who studied optical illusions.

bonuses.leadin: It is assessed by the MMPI and the "Big Five" test, which categorizes it into groups like "agreeableness" or "neuroticism". For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this reproductive gland that adds alkalinity to semen. It is affected by a cancer very common among older men that can be assessed with a rectal examination.

The ejaculatory duct that passes through the prostate forms from the union between the seminal vessel duct and this structure, which transports sperm away from the epididymis and is cut in a method of male contraception.

Prostatic secretions also contain trace amounts of this metal, which appears in the active sites of the enzymes carboxypeptidase, carbonic anhydrase, and alcohol dehydrogenase. Two cysteines and two histidines coordinate to it in a common structural motif.

bonuses.leadin: The anti-alpha 1 adrenergic receptor drugs tamsulosin and siludosin treat benign enlargments of this organ, which is homologous to Skene's glands in women. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This tern was used to designate privately funded adventurers who led military expeditions and tried to set up their own regimes in other countries. Examples include Narcisco Lopez who tried to take Cuba in 1848.

This brigadier general served as governor of Mexico City from 1847-48, during the American occupation, he was later indicted by the federal government for helping to support Lopez's filibustering attempts to conquer Cuba.

This Tennessee born former doctor began his filibustering career invading Sonora and actually captured Granada in 1856. He was eventually killed after he lost control of Nicaragua and tried one more attempt to conquer Central America.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about some crazy 19th century dudes, for ten points each:

parts.text: Name this artist who wrote "Honeysuckle Rose." He says he's "savin' all my love for you" in his "Ain't Misbehavin'."

Fats Waller played this instrument in the "stride" style. Art Tatum played his arrangements of "Tea for Two" and "Tiger Rag" on this instrument, which makes up a standard rhythm section with the bass and drummer.

"Honeysuckle Rose" and "Ain't Misbehavin'" have been recorded dozens of times by many bands, which is why they are known by this term. As an adjective, this word comes before "repertoire" when it is used to describe the canon of oft-performed classical music.

bonuses.leadin: This musician complains "your pedal extremities are colossal / To me, you look like a fossil" in "Your Feet's Too Big." For 10 points each:

parts.text: This principle states that no two electrons can have the same four quantum numbers n, l, m-sub-l, and m-sub-s.
This other principle dictates that it is impossible to simulatneously know the position and velocity of a individual particle. It is attributed to a German physicist.
These rules describe the order in which electrons fill an atom's suborbital shells. They are based on the Aufbau principle that electrons are added to the lowest avaliable energy shell of an atom.

bonuses.leadin: Answer some questons about elemetary quantum mechanics, for 10 points each:

parts.text: This is the thermodynamic potential of a system, usually denoted by a capital H.
This cycle, modeled on the heat engine of the same name, uses both isothermal and adiabatic expansion and compression to achieve the most efficient cycle possible.

This other cycle utilizes an organic working fluid that is heated to vaporization, expands to power a turbine, then condenses due to flowing water. The condensate returned to the evaporator to complete the thermodynamic cycle.

bonuses.leadin: Name these things from thermodynamics, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this novel whose title character makes a machine that causes reality to infinitely loop so that he can be with Faustine forever.
This author of The Invention of Morel was married to the gothic short-story writer Silvina Ocampo, whose sister Victoria published the magazine Sur.
Casares and the Ocampo sisters hail from this country, also the home of Julio Cortázar and Manuel Puig.

bonuses.leadin: The protagonist of this novel sees two suns and two moons as well as identical copies of dead fish. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this autoimmune disease that is nine times more common in women than men. This disease, nicknamed "the great imitator," presents with a characteristic butterfly-shaped rash on the face that resembles a wolf bite.

In this technique commonly used to diagnose lupus, antibody-antigen interactions are used to detect protein concentration in a liquid sample. The enzymes alkaline phosphatase and horseradish peroxidase are frequently used in this assay.

ELISA's ability to determine serum antibody concentration makes it useful in diagnosing these immune conditions that can lead to anaphylaxis. Peanuts, soy, and shellfish are often implicated in these conditions.
acceptableAnswers: accept specific types of allergies such as food allergies

bonuses.leadin: Anti-Smith and anti-nuclear antibodies can be used to detect this disease. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with alveoli structure and function.
What is the main function of the bronchus in the respiratory system?
Name another component of the respiratory system related to alveoli structure and function.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human respiratory system.

parts.text: Name this class of subatomic particles that obey Bose-Einstein statistics. They feature integer spin and are contrasted with fermions.
One of the four elementary bosons, these particles were described by Einstein as striking a metal and causing the emission of electrons.
This other class of subatomic particles has six "flavors": top, bottom, up, down, strange, and charm.

bonuses.leadin: The Higgs type of this class of subatomic particles is predicted to exist by the Standard Model. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this interval that spans from an A up to the next A. It is named because there are 8 scale degrees between those notes in a major or minor scale.
There are this many actual tones in an octave if you count all the notes in a chromatic scale. Serialist music requires all of these tones be played in a row before any of them are replayed.
This composer developed serialism as an outgrowth of his creation of atonal music, which he taught to his students Alban Berg and Anton von Webern.

bonuses.leadin: This interval, along with perfect fourths and perfect fifths, is generally avoided in parallel motion when part-writing. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this squire, who encounters his former neighbor Ricote when Ricote tries to recover his treasure. He rides the gray donkey Dapple.
Sancho Panza is the companion of this knight, the title character of a Cervantes novel. This character tilts at windmills that he mistakes for giants.
acceptableAnswers: The Ingenious Gentleman Don Quixote of La Mancha
El ingenioso hidalgo Don Quijote de La Mancha

parts.text: Don Quixote steals a barber's basin because he thinks it is this mythical object that belonged to a Moorish king.

bonuses.leadin: A duke and duchess offer this character the governorship of a fake island called Barataria. For 10 points each:
